blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Our previous analysis found that a model's native hashed N-gram table is where continual updates disturb the base least, but its writes needed backpropagation and changed the pretrained table. We present Delta N-gram, a forward-only write path into that table. The pretrained table T^0 is never modified. Evidence is written into a sparse patch Δon the rows it addresses: a 4.1M-parameter writer emits a target and a gate per (position, hash head) event, and a block-averaged delta rule keeps each row a convex combination of its old value and the gated targets. The writer is trained offline on raw text with the pretraining objective; at use time writing takes forward passes only, and clearing Δrestores the original model. A 0.6B prototype trained to answer questions keeps 16/16 facts after a second write; online gradient writes keep 2--4/16. We study two writers: a plain writer that encodes evidence with the T^0-only model, and a delta writer that reads its current memory while encoding. On Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, the plain writer's memory is document-specific: on 64 held-out news events it lowers continuation NLL by 0.068 nats/token against empty memory and by 0.024 against another document's memory, and 0.063 and 0.013 after 16 intervening articles. The delta writer's memory is more document-specific and keeps more of it under distraction (70% vs 54%). Over 35,000 writes on our previous seven-task chain both writers stay stable and the delta writer drifts less (layer-2 math drift 176% vs 188%); later accuracy changes by -0.26/-0.52pp (-7.29pp for gradient updates) and small-k_i drift is 17.9/17.5% (39.2%). Acquisition is negative, and general-input drift reaches 32.8% (20.75%): format rows read by every example grow to 4--12 times their pretrained norm. Zeroing eight such rows removes over 98% of layer-2 drift on math inputs, together with their NLL gain.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: A model that learns while it is used has to write new information somewhere, and every write is paid for by what it disturbs. In our previous work, Representation Drift [ 31 ] , we compared three places to write on the same 48-layer mixture-of-experts model: the rows of its native, pretrained hashed N-gram table [ 26 ] , one continually trained LoRA adapter [ 11 ] , and a fresh LoRA per task merged into the backbone. Updating only the N-gram table changed the base model’s representations of general inputs least (big- K K drift 26%/15% on math/code, against 64–97%/35–39% for LoRA), and this drift did not grow with the number of tasks. We concluded that long-running online learning should write new knowledge only into the memory table and keep the backbone fixed.
blocks.zh: 一个在使用时学习的模型必须写出新的信息到某个地方去,每个写作都要由它扰动的东西来支付. 在我们之前的作品"代表漂流 [31]"中,我们比较了三个位置来写在同一个48层的混合专家模型上:它的原生,经过预先训练的散列N克表的行 [26],一个不断训练的LORA适配器 [11],一个新鲜的LORA每个任务合并到骨干. 仅更新N-gram表就改变了基本模型对一般投入的表示最小(数学/代码上的大-K漂移为26%/15%,而LORA为64-97 %/35-39 %),这种漂移没有随着任务数量的增长而增加。 我们的结论是,长期在线学习应只将新知识写入内存表,并固定主干.

blocks.en: That conclusion was reached with an expensive and irreversible write. Every table update in [ 31 ] was an Adam step: a full backward pass through the network per write, optimizer state per row, labels to define the loss, and a table that, once changed, no longer contains its pretrained values. A system that writes continually during use needs the opposite properties. Writing should cost a forward pass, need no labels or task boundaries, and leave the pretrained knowledge recoverable.
blocks.zh: 以昂贵和不可逆转的文字得出了这一结论。 在 [31] 中的每个表格更新都是亚当步骤:一个完全后向的通过网络每写,每行优化状态,标签来定义损失,一个表格一旦改变,就不再包含其被预先训练的值. 一个在使用期间持续写作的系统需要相反的属性. 写作应该花费前行通行证,不需要标签或任务界限,并且让预先训练的知识可以收回.

blocks.en: This paper builds that write path. We keep the pretrained table T 0 T^{0} fixed and write into a sparse patch Δ \Delta , so the model reads T 0 + Δ T^{0}+\Delta . A small writer, trained offline, turns each block of evidence into writes. For every event, that is, every (position, hash head) pair, it emits a target v v and a gate β \beta from the frozen model’s hidden states. Events that address the same row in a block are averaged and applied with a delta rule we call D1. D1 moves the row toward the gated targets and keeps it a convex combination of its old value and those targets. Seen from linear attention, this is a DeltaNet [ 27 , 32 ] whose keys are one-hot hash addresses, whose state is never reset, and whose write targets come from a learned fast-weight programmer [ 28 ] . The writer is trained with the pretraining objective on raw text. Each document is split into chunks; each chunk is first predicted from the memory written so far and then written, and the loss of later chunks backpropagates through the whole chain of writes. At use time the same writer and the same D1 run forward only.
blocks.zh: 本文构建了写道. 我们保留预训表 T 0 T^{0} 固定并写入一个稀疏的补丁 Δ\ Delta, 所以模型读取 T 0 + Δ T^{0}+\ 德尔塔。 一个小作家,训练有素的离线,把每一块证据都变成了写作. 每个事件, 即每对(位置, 散列头), 在一个区块中处理同一行的事件是平均的,并适用三角洲规则,我们称之为D1。 D1将一行移向有门的目标,并保持了它原有价值和那些目标的对流结合. 从线性注意来看,这是一款DeltaNet[27,32],其密钥为单热散列地址,其状态从未被重置,其写作目标出自于已学快重程序员[28]. 编剧接受关于原始文字的预训目标的培训. 每个文档被分割成块;每个块首先从迄今为止所写的内存中预测出,然后写出,然后通过整个写作链块的后方块回传被丢失. 在使用时,同名编剧和同名D1只向前跑.

blocks.en: The writer must read the evidence before it writes, and we study two ways of doing so. The plain writer encodes evidence with the model reading only T 0 T^{0} . Its targets are then anchored to the evidence, rows stay separable, and all blocks of a document can be encoded in one batch. The delta writer encodes evidence with the model reading its current memory, so what it writes can depend on what it has already stored. That is what long-term continual learning ultimately needs, for instance to connect a new report to an entity written earlier. Its price is sequential writing and a feedback loop through the memory. We analyse that loop and train both writers on the same data.
blocks.zh: 作家在写作前必须先阅读证据,我们研究两种方法. 平面写作器将证据编码,模型只读取了T 0 T^{0}. 其目标随后被锁定在证据上,行会保持可分,文件的所有块都可以被编码成一批. 三角洲作家用模型读取其当前内存来编码证据,所以它所写的可以取决于它已经存储的内容. 这就是长期持续学习最终需要的,例如,将一份新报告与一个先前编写的实体联系起来。 其价格为相继写作并贯穿内存反馈回路. 我们分析这个循环 并训练两位作家使用相同的数据。

blocks.en: We train both writers (4.1M parameters each) on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (512 experts, 48 layers) for 100M target tokens. We evaluate them on held-out news events, on the seven-task chain of [ 31 ] , and on LoCoMo [ 20 ] . 1. Trained to answer, forward writes bind and keep facts, but only in the trained form. On a 0.6B prototype trained with a question-answering objective, the writer keeps 16 of 16 facts after a second write, where online gradient writes into the same table keep 2–4. With a paraphrased question it stays at the empty-memory level ( Section 6.1 ). 2. Raw-text training yields document-specific memory. On 64 late-2025 news events, reading a document’s own memory beats reading another document’s, which beats empty memory, at every training stage. At 100M tokens the two gains are 0.068 and 0.024 nats/token, and 0.063 and 0.013 after 16 intervening articles ( Section 6 ). 3. Reading memory while encoding changes how the writer writes. The delta writer’s memory is more specific to its document ( Δ donor \Delta_{\mathrm{donor}} 0.032 against 0.023 without distractors) and keeps more of that specificity after 16 distractors (70% against 54%); its total gain over empty memory on these news events is smaller. A weight × \times encoding factorial places this change in the learned weights ( Section 6.5 ). On the seven-task chain the delta writer drifts less than the plain writer: math drift is 176% against 188% at layer 2 and 40.2% against 41.8% at the head. It also answers slightly more (129 against 125 of 448 test items, and 112 against 103 written examples) ( Section 7 ). 4. Long write chains are stable. Both writers, including the delta writer whose encoding feeds back through its own memory, made 35,000 consecutive writes on two hardware stacks without numerical failure ( Section 7 ). 5. What was stored changes little afterwards, but little is stored. After each task is written, learned-task accuracy changes by − 0.26 -0.26 pp (plain) and − 0.52 -0.52 pp (delta) over the rest of the chain, against − 7.29 -7.29 pp for the Adam table updates of [ 31 ] . Small- k i k_{i} drift at the head input is 17.9% and 17.5%, against 39.2%. Net acquisition on these tasks, which the writer never saw, is negative ( − 12 / 448 -12/448 ), and recall of written examples is 23–25% ( Section 7 ). 6. Drift concentrates on a few hot rows and can be located. General-input big- K K drift is 32.8%, 1.6 times that of [ 31 ] . It enters at the injection layer through eight format bigram rows that every example writes, whose patches reach 4.4–11.7 times ‖ T 0 ‖ \left\lVert T^{0}\right\rVert . Zeroing them removes over 98% of the layer-2 drift on math inputs and also removes their NLL gain ( Section 8 ).

blocks.en: Our previous work, Representation Drift [ 31 ] , compared update channels on the model we use and found that writing only into the native N-gram table perturbs general inputs least; its costs were interference among stored tasks and weak acquisition. This paper keeps that channel and replaces the write: forward instead of gradient, patch instead of in-place change. Forgetting under sequential fine-tuning [ 22 , 14 , 19 , 2 ] and subspace constraints on successive updates [ 6 , 30 , 17 ] motivate the comparison but act on dense parameters, not on addressed rows.
blocks.zh: 我们之前的作品"代表漂流"[31],比较了我们使用的模型的更新频道,发现只写入本地N-克表的扰动一般输入最少;其成本是存储任务中的干扰和获取薄弱. 本文保留了该通道并取代了写入:前行而不是渐变,补丁而不是就地更改. 在相继微调[22,14,19,2]和相继更新的子空间限制[6,30,17]下被遗忘,激发了比较的动力,但对密集参数采取行动,而不是在地址行.

blocks.en: Linear attention can be read as a fast-weight memory written by a slow network [ 28 , 27 ] . DeltaNet replaces additive writes with error-correcting delta writes [ 27 , 32 ] . Gated DeltaNet adds a scalar decay [ 33 ] , and KDA makes the decay channel-wise [ 13 ] . Test-time training generalises the inner update to a learned objective [ 29 ] . Qwen3.8 itself contains such layers. These lines address interference among keys in a finite state that is cleared at the end of each sequence, which is why they need decay. Our keys are one-hot hash addresses over hundreds of millions of rows, the state persists across requests, and the writer is added to a frozen pretrained model rather than trained with it. Decay in our setting pulls toward T 0 T^{0} rather than toward zero ( Section 3.5 ).
blocks.zh: 线性注意力可以被读取为慢网络所写的快重记忆 [28, 27]. 德尔塔 网易替代添加剂用错误校正三角洲写出 [27,32]. 三角洲 Net会增加一个分级衰变[33],而KDA会使衰变通道顺着[13]. 试训时间概括了内在更新到所学目标[29]. Quen3.8本身就含有这样的层. 这些线条处理键之间的干扰,在一个有限度的状态下,在每个序列末端被清除,这就是它们需要衰变的原因. 我们的钥匙是一热散列的地址 超过数亿行, 状态坚持在各种要求, 编剧被添加到一个被冻结的 预先训练的模型中, 我们环境的衰变使T 0 T^{0}而不是零 (第3.5节)。

blocks.en: Sparse Delta Memory [ 3 ] enlarges the state of a gated linear RNN with an explicit memory whose slots are selected by product keys and written with a gated delta rule. Fast-weight product-key memory [ 34 ] updates the values of a product-key memory by chunk-level gradient descent on a reconstruction loss, at training and at inference time, and can carry them across adjacent segments. Both are layers trained together with the backbone, over learned keys. Ours adds a writer to a frozen pretrained model, writes into a table the model was pretrained to read, and uses no gradients at use time.
blocks.zh: Sparse Delta Memory [3] 扩展了有门的线性RNN的状态,带有一个明确的内存,其槽由产品键选择,并用有门的三角地规则来写出. 快速量产-键内存[34]通过块级梯度下降来更新重建损失上,培训和推断时间上的产品-键内存的值,并可以把它们携带到相邻部分. 这两层都是与骨干一起训练的,超乎所学的钥匙. 我们把一个编剧添加到一个被冷冻的预先训练的模型中,写入一个表格中,这个模型被预先训练去读取,使用时没有使用梯度.

blocks.en: Memory and product-key layers provide large sparsely addressed stores [ 15 , 1 ] . Sparse memory finetuning updates only rows selected by their access statistics and forgets less than LoRA or full fine-tuning [ 18 , 9 ] . EngramEdit writes facts into the N-gram embeddings of LongCat-Flash-Lite with a closed-form ridge solution and a penalty on reused rows [ 4 ] . ENGRAFT optimises the Engram rows of Qwen3.8-Flash-Next by gradient descent with a KL constraint and keeps the result as a removable overlay [ 7 ] . All of these compute the write from labelled facts or tasks, by backpropagation or a solve. Ours writes from raw evidence in a forward pass, with no labels, into a separable patch. Knowledge editing in FFN weights [ 23 , 24 , 5 ] shares the key–value view we use for drift but edits dense projections.
blocks.zh: 内存和出品键层提供大量零星的商店[15, 1]. Sparse内存微调只按其访问统计数据所选择的行进行更新,并忘记了小于LORA或全微调[18,9]. 图标 编辑将事实写入"长卡特-快克-快克-快克"(LongCat-Flash-Lite)的N-gram嵌入中,并使用封闭式的山脊溶液并处罚被再利用的行 [4]. ENGRAFT通过带有KL约束的梯度降入来选择Qune3.8-Flash-Next的Engram行并保留可移动上覆[7]的结果. 所有这些都通过反向传播或解答,从贴有标签的事实或任务中计算出书写. 我们的从原始证据写在前传,没有标签,变成可分隔的补丁. 在FFN权重中的知识编辑[23, 24, 5] 分享我们用来漂移的键值视图,

blocks.en: The closest work is MemT-1.0 [ 16 ] . It also freezes the backbone, writes a per-user memory forward-only and trains the memory module offline. Its memory is a set of added blocks with dense GDN-2 state, routed over storage experts, updated token by token and committed per turn. It trains 0.45–3.6B parameters on 34B tokens: continued pretraining, then post-training that distils from the frozen backbone given the full history. Post-training adds about 10.69 points over the continued-pretraining checkpoint, the largest effect in its ablations. Our memory is the model’s own N-gram table, read through its native injection, with a 4M-parameter writer trained on 100M raw-text tokens. Because the state is a sparse patch on known rows, its drift can be traced to individual rows ( Section 8 ). MemT’s results on long-conversation benchmarks [ 20 ] show what a trained cross-position objective buys. Our LoCoMo failure ( Section 7.5 ) is consistent with that, and its full-context teacher is the first change we would borrow ( Section 9 ).
blocks.zh: 最接近的作品是MemT-1.0 [16]. 它还会冻结骨干,只写出每个用户的内存前行并训练出内存模块下线. 它的内存是一组加成的块,具有密集的GDN-2状态,路由于存储专家,以符号更新符号并每转弯承诺. 它在34B符上训练了0.45–3.6B参数:持续进行前训练,然后进行后训练,从被冻结的骨干中提取出完整的历史. 训练后检查站比继续训练的检查站增加了约10.69分,这是检查站爆炸的最大影响。 我们的记忆是该模型自己的N克表,通过本作的注入读取,有一个4M参数的写作员受过100M原始文字符号的训练. 由于状态在已知行上是稀有的补丁,其漂移可以被追溯到单个行上(第8节. MemT关于长对话基准的结果显示, 我们的LoCoMo失败(第7.5节)与此一致,它的全文老师是我们借用的第一个变化(第9节)。

blocks.en: The frozen model runs over the block, and we take the input of the LM head, normalised by a parameter-free RMSNorm (Qwen3.8 has no separate final norm, and the per-token scale of this input varies widely): H ^ t = N ⁡ ( E ⁡ ( x t , T 0 + λ ​ Δ t ) ) , λ ∈ { 0 , 1 } , \hat{H}_{t}=\mathrm{N}\big(E(x_{t};\,T^{0}+\lambda\Delta_{t})\big),\qquad\lambda\in\{0,1\}, (6) with gradients stopped at H ^ t \hat{H}_{t} . With λ = 0 \lambda=0 the evidence is encoded by the model with an empty patch; we call this T 0 T^{0} -only encoding and the writer trained with it the plain writer . blocks.en: The writer is trained on raw text with next-token prediction, the same objective as pretraining, and needs no labels or question–answer data. 1. A document, or a time-ordered stream of reports on one event, is split into blocks of 512 tokens. Each query carries the last 128 tokens of the previous block as prefix. 2. Memory starts empty. The loss is normalised once by the number of target tokens in the whole training group and backpropagated through the full chain of writes; only θ \theta receives gradients. The gradient path is: loss → \to frozen layers above the injection → \to native read-out ( 2 )–( 4 ) → \to patch Δ t \Delta_{t} → \to D1 chain ( 5 ) → \to writer ( 8 ). Stopping gradients at H ^ t \hat{H}_{t} removes the branch “old memory → \to encoding → \to features” under memory-aware encoding. This is a truncation of backpropagation through time, chosen for cost: the forward dynamics, and hence the agreement between training and use, are unchanged.

blocks.en: Before the native model we develop the method on a frozen 0.6B model with an external, zero-initialised hash table ( T 0 = 0 T^{0}=0 ): 16,384 rows each for bigrams and trigrams, row width 1024. The two orders are summed, divided by 2 \sqrt{2} and injected before decoder layer 1. The prototype went through two stages that differ in the training objective. • Question-answering objective. On Qwen3-0.6B-Base, the writer is trained on synthetic episodes. Short evidence blocks stating facts about named entities are written one at a time, and the loss is placed on the answers to template questions about them. Training uses 2,000 episodes (500 outer steps, seed 17), with disjoint entity pools for training and evaluation. Evaluation generates answers greedily on 16 held-out worlds with two writes each. It compares the writer with online gradient writes into the same table (ten SparseAdam steps per evidence block, learning rate 0.01 or 0.05), the full evidence in context, and BM25 retrieval of the top two blocks. Transfer probes, without retraining, test a paraphrased question that keeps the entity name, chains of 4 and 16 writes, and revision of an earlier value. • Raw-text objective. The writer is then trained as in Section 3.4 , on raw text with no question–answer data, on the post-trained Qwen3-0.6B (1,190,465 writer parameters, hidden width 128). A 5M-token code-only pilot with two seeds comes first, followed by a 100M-token run on the five-source mixture described below. A matched 5M-token run on the base model tests whether a writer transfers between the two readers. Prototype and native results are reported separately throughout.

The first scoring window , the up to 384 targets right after the 128-token context, tests whether the gain is present before the later report has unfolded. A prefix split separates families whose 128-token context restates the early facts (34), does not (23) or is unclear (7). A direction-permutation control permutes the channels of the read-out vector at scoring time, preserving addresses, counts and row norms, to test whether the gain comes from what was written.

Intervals are percentile intervals from 10,000 family-paired bootstrap resamples; comparisons across checkpoints resample the same families. The pretraining cutoff of Qwen3.8 is not documented, so the model may have seen these events; the empty condition measures what it already knows.
For the prototype we also report a historical held-out set of 640 families from the five sources, scored the same way and macro-averaged over sources.

blocks.en: 5.3 Seven-task chain

blocks.en: We reuse the seven morphological inflection tasks of [ 31 ] , drawn from SIGMORPHON [ 8 ] , in the order SME → \to NAV → \to HYE → \to AFB → \to SQI → \to MKD → \to AMH. Each task contributes 5,000 support examples (prompt and reference answer, in the chat template with thinking disabled), the same examples and exposures as the 125 Adam steps × \times batch 40 of [ 31 ] . Every example is one evidence document and one D1 update, so a chain makes 35,000 writes. One state is kept for the whole chain: it is never cleared or partitioned at task boundaries, and the writer is frozen and was never tuned on these tasks. The tasks’ earlier results motivated this work, so this is a re-test on historical tasks, not a fresh benchmark.
blocks.zh: 我们重用从SIGMORPHON [8] 从SME → NAV → → CHYE → AFB → SQI → MKD → AMH 中抽取的7个形态活性任务。 每项任务贡献了5000个支持实例(即时和参考答案,在与思维被禁用的聊天模板中),与125 Adam steps ×\times 第40批 [31] 相同的例子和曝光. 每个例子都是一份证据文件和一份D1更新,所以一连串可以使35000作文. 一个状态为整个链条所保留:它从未在任务边界被清除或分割,而写作器被冻结并从未被调用过这些任务. 这些任务之前的成果推动了这项工作,因此这是对历史任务的再测试,而不是新的基准。

blocks.en: Evaluation follows [ 31 ] : • Accuracy : 64 fixed test items per task, greedy decoding of at most 128 new tokens, exact match after stripping and Unicode NFC normalisation. Each task is also tested before its support examples are written, so that acquisition is measured as the change from writing. • Answer NLL : teacher-forced NLL of the reference answers. • Drift : representations at the last prompt token at all 48 layers (four residual streams concatenated, 10,240 dimensions) and at the LM-head input (2,560 dimensions), as relative RMS change. Big- K K drift uses 128 math and 64 code probes against the empty state; small- k i k_{i} drift compares each task’s probes with the state right after that task was written. • Seen-example recall : 448 support examples already written (64 per task) are answered from the final state. The three arms of [ 31 ] (N-gram table trained with Adam, shared LoRA, merged LoRA) are reused, not rerun.

blocks.en: 5.4 LoCoMo
blocks.zh: 5.4 可可

blocks.en: LoCoMo [ 20 ] has 10 long dialogues and 1,986 questions; we use the delta writer. Each dialogue is written once into an empty memory, in session order, rendered as text with a dated header per session and one “Speaker: utterance” line per turn, in 512-token blocks. All questions of a dialogue are answered from the same written state, which questions do not modify. Four conditions use the same question prompt: self (own dialogue in memory, only the question in context), empty , donor (another dialogue of similar length in memory) and full context (empty memory, the whole dialogue in context). The prompt instructs the model to answer “No information available” when it lacks the information. Decoding is greedy with at most 32 new tokens. The three memory conditions read through the FP32 split read-out of Appendix A . The full-context condition needs no patch and runs the native BF16 read-out with expert offloading, so the two kinds of condition use numerically different read paths. The main score is LoCoMo’s category-aware token F1 on the 1,540 questions of categories 1–4; the 446 adversarial questions are excluded. We also score the teacher-forced NLL of the reference answers. We do not compare these numbers directly with [ 16 ] , which uses a different backbone, prompts and judging.

blocks.en: 6 Document-Specific Memory from Raw Text

blocks.en: On the native model the writer only ever sees raw-text continuation. This section first traces how the prototype arrived at that objective. It then asks whether raw text is enough for the writer to learn memory that is specific to the document written, robust to later writes, and carried by the content of the patch.

blocks.en: Trained to answer questions, the forward writer binds facts and keeps them ( Table 2 ). One write raises answer accuracy from the empty-memory 2/16 to 16/16. After a second write all 16 first facts are still answered, and 15 of the 16 new ones. Online gradient writes into the same table learn each new fact but overwrite the old one, keeping only 2–4 of 16. The forward writer matches putting the evidence in context and retrieving it with BM25. This is the contrast that motivates the method: writing by gradient into shared rows forgets, while a learned forward write need not.
blocks.zh: 接受过回答问题的培训,前行作家将事实捆绑起来并保存下来(表2)。 一出写法从空相2/16到16/16提高了答案的准确性. 在第二次写完之后,所有16个最初的事实仍然得到回答,16个新事实中有15个得到答复。 在线梯度写入同一张表格,学习每个新事实,但覆盖了旧事实,只保留了16个中的2-4个. 前置写手将证据放入上下文,并用BM25取回. 这就是激励方法的对比:用梯度来写入共享行会忘记,而学习到的向前写则不需要.

blocks.en: The same experiments expose the limits that reappear on the native model. • The binding is tied to the trained question form. Asked with a paraphrased question that still names the entity, the writer stays at the empty-memory 2/16 before and after writing. The rows read by such queries overlap the written rows in only about 6% of positions. • Longer chains erode it. Without retraining, four writes leave 60 of 64 facts answerable. After sixteen writes, 46 of 64 are answered right after their own write but only 19 at the end. Revised values are followed immediately in 5 of 16 worlds. • Template rows carry a trade-off. At an earlier checkpoint, two old answers were lost after the second write. Restoring the ten rows of the literal question template to their values before that write rescues both old answers (14 to 16), but new answers fall from 12 to 2. These are the same shared rows that, on the native model, carry both gain and drift ( Section 8 ). A question-answering objective also needs labelled episodes in a fixed format. We therefore moved to the pretraining objective, which needs no labels and applies to any text.

blocks.en: The seven-task chain puts the writer far outside its training distribution. Training trajectories have at most 32 blocks of raw text. Here a single state receives 35,000 writes of short, templated examples from tasks the writer has never seen. This section reports what the chain does to stability, to what is stored, to what is acquired and to the base.

blocks.en: Both writers completed 35,000 consecutive writes on both stacks without numerical failure. The delta writer gives 17.5%. The comparison holds at matched rounds. For SME after one, two and three further tasks: 12.8%, 18.7% and 19.4%, against 32.5%, 40.1% and 41.6%. For NAV after one and two further tasks: 16.3% and 17.2%, against 50.8% and 51.8%. Inside the network the picture differs: at layer 9, four of the six tasks drift by more than 180%. The small output-side drift sits on top of large early-layer changes.
blocks.zh: 在头部输入中,学习到的任务平均从自己写作结束到链条结束漂移了17.9%(表6),而N克臂为[31]39.2%. 三角洲作家给予17.5%. 比较以相匹配的回合进行。 对一、二和三项任务之后的中小企业:12.8%、18.7%和19.4%,分别为32.5%、40.1%和41.6%。 在完成另外一项和两项任务之后,NAV:16.3%和17.2%,而50.8%和51.8%。 网络内部的图片不同:在第9层,6个任务中有4个漂移了180%以上. 小型输出侧漂移坐落在大型早期变化之上.

blocks.en: On general inputs the chain drifts more than the N-gram arm of [ 31 ] . At the head input, math probes drift by 41.8% and code probes by 23.8% from the empty state (mean 32.8%), against 26%/15% (mean 20.75%) for that arm. This is still below merged LoRA (49.67%) and shared LoRA (68.12%). The two probe sets reach this level in different ways: • Math drift enters at the injection. It is 0 at layer 1, before the injection, and 198% at layer 2 after the first task; it then decays with depth to 42.5% at the head. It is fully present after the first task (5,000 writes) and does not accumulate: after the seventh task it is 188% at layer 2 and 41.8% at the head. • Code drift is 1–3% at layer 2 and builds up in later layers through attention, reaching 24% at the head. The math pattern is what a few hot rows read directly at the probe position would produce, and Section 8 confirms it. Big- K K drift is not a behavioural loss here: math answer NLL falls from 0.904 (empty) to 0.846, and code NLL is unchanged (0.247 to 0.246). The rows that move the math representations also help predict the math answers ( Section 8.2 ). We nevertheless count 32.8% as a defect. Drift on general inputs is a budget the method must stay within, not a cost to be offset by gains.

blocks.en: Weak acquisition could mean the state stores the examples but does not generalise from them. We test this directly. From the final states, both writers answer the same 448 support examples that were written into memory (64 per task), using their original prompts. The plain writer answers 103/448 (22.99%) and the delta writer 112/448 (25.00%). The difference is +9 items (paired McNemar p = 0.049 p=0.049 , uncorrected, exploratory). Neither state reproduces a large share of what it was given, so the data do not support “remembered but not generalised”. The writes did not bind each answer to an address from which the answer can be read back ( Section 8.3 ).

blocks.en: 8.3 The answer entry
blocks.zh: 第8.3条 答案条目

blocks.en: The same audit explains part of the failure to use memory at a different position. In both the seven-task prompts and the LoCoMo prompts, the first answer token is predicted at the end of the chat template, after </think> and two newlines. All 448 recall prompts of Section 7.4 and all 1,986 LoCoMo questions read the same 16 physical rows there. • In the seven-task chain the support examples use the same template, so these 16 rows are written throughout the chain. Answers to different lemmas and features meet in the same rows, where later writes can mix with or overwrite earlier ones. • In LoCoMo, the dialogue text written into memory contains no template, so in all ten dialogue states these 16 rows were never written: their patches and counts are zero. Across the 426 blocks and 3.4 million address events of the dialogues, no write lands on them. Memory can still reach the first answer token, but only indirectly: patches read at earlier prompt positions must propagate through attention and the convolution. The writer was trained on raw-text continuation, where the useful pattern is to write at a position and read at the same n-gram later. It was never trained to make content written in one context readable from an answer position whose own rows carry nothing. A plausible explanation for both the weak recall of Section 7.4 and the LoCoMo result is therefore this: the writer learned to write and read at the same position, while question answering needs retrieval across positions. We regard this as the main open problem of the method rather than a property of the addressing alone. The writer’s features include right context and a block-level pool, so it can see the answer when it writes earlier rows, and queries can attend to rows read earlier in the prompt.
blocks.zh: 同一审计也解释了在不同的位置未能使用内存的部分原因. 在"七任务提示"和"LoCoMo提示"中,第一个答案符被预测在聊天模板的结尾,在"/think"和两条新行后. - 所有448个召回第7.4节的提示,所有1 986个LoCoMo问题都读到同样的16行。 在七任务链中,支持示例使用相同的模板,因此这16行被写入整个链中. 对不同的lemma和特征的回答在同一行相会相会,后面的写作可以和前作相混合或覆盖. ^ 在"LoCoMo"中,被写入内存的对话框文本没有模板,所以在所有10个对话框中都声明这16行从未被写入:他们的补丁和计数为零. 在426个街区和340万个对话活动上,没有文字记录。 记忆仍然可以到达第一个答案符号,但只是间接的:在更早的即时位置所读取的补丁必须通过注意和分解来传播. 编剧接受了关于原始文本续作的培训,其中有用的模式是在某个位置写作,并在后期读取同正克. 它从未受过训练,使在一个上下文中写的内容能够从自己一行无所事事的回答位置读取。 因此,对7.4节和LoCoMo结果的微弱召回的一个合理解释是:作者学会在同一位置写作和阅读,而回答问题则需要跨位置检索。 我们认为,这是方法方面的主要公开问题,而不只是解决问题的财产。 编剧的功能包括右上下文和一个块级池,因此在写出更早的行时可以看到答案,而查询可以处理在快取中较早读取的行.

blocks.en: In LoCoMo, the dialogue text written into memory contains no template, so in all ten dialogue states these 16 rows were never written: their patches and counts are zero. Across the 426 blocks and 3.4 million address events of the dialogues, no write lands on them.

blocks.en: 9 Discussion
blocks.zh: 9 讨论情况

blocks.en: The native N-gram table is sparse and addressable, and the model already reads it. Writing there needs no new memory module, no change to the backbone and no external store. If future models ship with such tables, the table may be the natural place for continual learning: a writable store of knowledge inside the model that leaves the backbone untouched.
blocks.zh: 原生的N-gram表是稀有和可地址的,模型已经读取了. 写到那里不需要新的内存模块,没有主干线的更改,也没有外部商店. 如果未来的模型带有这些表,表可能是继续学习的自然地所在:模型内可写作的知识储存,使骨干不受影响。

blocks.en: Exact-token addresses are what make the method’s retention and attribution possible. A write touches only the rows its n-grams address, and an input whose prefix reads none of them is unchanged. The same property limits use. A row can only help when the same n-gram is read again, so content written at one position is not directly available at another; Section 8.3 shows the answer position reading rows that were never written. Content addressing would give binding, but writes would overlap again, and with overlap comes interference. This is the central trade-off of the approach. Our results suggest that what is missing is a writer trained to make written content usable across positions, and possibly a memory module with its own attention for reading it (see the last paragraph of this section). The next step is an episodic objective, in which evidence is written and then queried at other positions, with distillation from the same frozen model given the evidence in context. That distillation is the component whose removal costs MemT the most [ 16 ] . A CPU check on existing LoCoMo losses can decide first whether the n-grams of the answers are reachable at all, or whether a small content-addressed memory is needed beside the table.
blocks.zh: 准确的地址是使这种方法得以保留和归属的原因。 写作只触及行的正克地址,而前缀读取的输入则无一不变. 同一财产限制使用。 一行只有在同一个n-克再次被读取时才能有所帮助,所以在一个位置所写的内容在另一个位置不能直接取用; 第8.3节显示了从未被写入的答案位置读取行. 内容的处理将产生约束力,但写作会再次重叠,而重叠则会产生干扰。 这是方法的中心取舍。 我们的结果表明,所缺少的是一名作家,他受过培训,可以使书面内容在各种立场之间发挥效用,并可能有一个内存单元,由自己注意阅读(见本节最后一段)。 下一步是一个偶发目标,即撰写证据,然后在其他位置询问,从同一被冻结的模型中提取证据。 蒸馏是MemT最需要去除的成分 [16]. CPU对现有LoCoMo损失的检查可以首先决定答案的正克是否完全可以被达到,或者在表格外是否需要一个小的内容地址内存.

blocks.en: Pretrained knowledge is the most valuable thing the model has, so absolute drift on general inputs must be bounded and not traded against gains. The method already makes drift locatable: we know which rows moved, how far and through which tokens. The default should therefore include a per-row cap, Δ j ← Δ j ⋅ min ⁡ ( 1 , c ​ ‖ T j 0 ‖ ‖ Δ j ‖ + ε ) , \Delta_{j}\leftarrow\Delta_{j}\cdot\min\!\Big(1,\ \frac{c\,\left\lVert T^{0}_{j}\right\rVert}{\left\lVert\Delta_{j}\right\rVert+\varepsilon}\Big), (16) with c c fixed in advance by the drift budget for big K K and small k i k_{i} , not tuned for gains. Since the read-out is injected at layer 2, bounding each patch relative to its pretrained row bounds the perturbation at the injection directly. Section 8.2 shows the cost: the hot rows also carry the generic gain, and zeroing them removes it; how much of it a nonzero cap keeps is untested. Recovering gains inside the budget is the role of multi-slot rows . The few most-written rows would get several slots keyed by context, so that a generic signal and specific content are stored apart and used only where the context matches; all other rows keep a single value. A larger hash table does not help, because it removes collisions but not the sharing of one n-gram by many contexts. For the plain writer, the effect of locking any set of rows can be computed from existing final states. A cap enforced during writing needs only the write chains of the capped rows to be replayed.

blocks.en: Encoding evidence with the T 0 T^{0} -only model is a choice, not a necessity. It anchors targets to the evidence, keeps rows separable, makes training and use identical, and lets all blocks be encoded in one batch, which on Qwen3.8 is the difference between about 3,200 and 940 target tokens per second. The cost is that the writer cannot interpret new content in the light of what it has stored, for instance resolving a pronoun to an entity written earlier. Memory-aware encoding removes that limitation. It serialises writing and makes the state sensitive to small numerical differences, though in our measurements these stayed on a bounded plateau below read-side noise ( Section 6.5 ). The factorial shows that training with it changes how the writer writes. Over 35,000 writes, the resulting writer drifts less than the plain writer, most clearly in early layers, with slightly higher accuracy and recall ( Section 7.3 ). On news continuation it trades total gain for document specificity. The two writers therefore remain two lines of the method. The plain writer gives batch training, row-level attribution and reproducibility. The delta writer is the route to integrating new evidence with what is already stored. What it still lacks is a training signal that rewards such integration: evidence spread over several related documents, with corrections and revisions, rather than continuation of one document at a time.
blocks.zh: 与 T0 T^{0 } 编码证据 - 只有模型是选择, 而不是必要 。 它将目标锁定在证据上,保持行相分离,使训练与使用完全相同,并让所有区块被编码成一批,这在Quen3.8上是每秒约3200个和940个目标令牌的相差. 其代价是,作者不能根据其所储存的内容来解释新内容,例如,将代名词解决给一个先前写的实体。 记忆意识编码消除了这种限制. 它将文字序列化,使状态对小的数值差异敏感,尽管在我们测量中这些数值停留在读边噪音下方的有界高地上(第6.5节)。 要素显示训练会改变作家的写作方式。 超过三万五千篇的写作,产生的写作者漂移得比平庸的写作者要少,最明显的是在早期分层,精度和回想略高(第7.3节. 在新闻续作时,它以全部收益换取文件的特异性。 因此,这两个作者仍然是方法的两行. 平庸作家提供分批培训,行级归属和再生. 三角洲作家是将新证据与已经储存的东西相融合的路线. 目前仍然缺乏的是一个鼓励这种整合的培训信号:证据分散在几个相关文件上,有更正和修改,而不是每次继续一个文件。

blocks.en: Every token of the evidence produces write events; how much each writes is decided by the learned gate, not by hand-written masks. Raw-text training teaches the writer what helps later continuation. It does not teach what a later question will need, and it does not teach restraint on format rows that every example shares. The one boundary still set by hand is what counts as evidence. User documents, user corrections and verified outcomes count. The model’s own generations are not written back by default, because a persistent write that conditions all of a user’s later requests is where self-reinforcement would do damage.
blocks.zh: 证据的每个符号都会产生写作事件;每个写作的多少由学门决定,而不是由手写口罩决定. 原始文字训练教给编剧什么有助于以后的续作. 它没有教导后期的问题需要什么,也没有教每个例子共享的格式行的限制. 仍然由手定出的唯一边界就是证据。 用户文件、用户更正和核实结果计数。 模式本身的几代人并不是默认地写回的,因为一个持久地写着,一个用户后来的所有要求都以自我加强会造成损害为条件。

blocks.en: Each user’s memory is a separable set of sparse rows, so it can be kept on the client and supplied per request, while the backbone and writer are shared. A dialogue of 13,000–25,000 tokens gives 78–145 MB of FP32 rows before any compression. A client can only change its own state; merging the patches of many users into a shared one is where privacy and poisoning questions arise. A portable state must carry its compatibility information: the backbone, tokenizer and writer versions, the addressing scheme, the write operator and decay, and a schema and layout version with a content checksum. A resumable full state, with counts and clock, must be distinguished from a read-only snapshot for inference.
blocks.zh: 每个用户的内存是一组可分离的稀有行,因此可以保存在客户端上并按请求提供,而骨干和编剧则共享. 13,000–25,000个令牌的对话框在压缩前会给出78–145个FP32行的MB. 一个客户端只能改变自己的状态;将许多用户的补丁合并为一个共享的补丁就是出现隐私和中毒问题的地方. 便携式状态必须携带其相容性信息:主干,活化器和写作机版本,地址方案,写操作符和衰变,以及带有内容校验和的图案和布局版本. 具有计数和时钟的可恢复的完整状态必须与只读快照区分开来推论.

blocks.en: The method is the fast half of a two-speed system. In use, it writes sparse rows quickly. During a “sleep” phase, signals that have proved stable and general, such as the generic gain now carried by hot rows, would be consolidated into a protected shared part, and specific content would stay in sparse rows. This is the division of labour between hippocampus and neocortex in complementary learning systems [ 21 ] , and the starting point of our 2023 work on online LoRA updates with sleep cycles. A forward write path is also what a self-improving system needs: the model writes its experience into its own memory and works with that memory afterwards. Connecting the two is the subject of our next paper.

blocks.en: Two experiments show that the method does not yet work on long-chain tasks that need written content at a different position. On the seven-task chain, net acquisition is negative and only 23–25% of written examples can be recalled. On LoCoMo, every memory condition answers with the same refusal. Our writers went through only the first half of MemT-1.0’s recipe [ 16 ] : continuation on raw text (100M tokens), with no post-training. MemT follows its 20B tokens of continued pretraining with 14B tokens of post-training on memory-specific data, distilled from the frozen backbone given the full history. That stage adds about 10.69 points in its ablation, and it targets exactly the cross-position use our writers lack. Hot rows have no budget relative to their pretrained norms, and general-input drift is 1.6 times that of the N-gram arm of [ 31 ] . Budget limited us to one model with a native N-gram table. We did not train writers for LongCat-Flash-Lite, the model edited by EngramEdit [ 4 ] , which adds its n-gram embeddings at the input without a gate. Nor did we train one for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017, which injects two tables at different layers. A writer is tied to its backbone, so each would need its own; the second would also test the drift bound with more than one injection point. All results come from one training seed.
blocks.zh: 两项实验表明,该方法尚不能用于不同位置需要书面内容的长链任务. 在7个任务链上,净收购是负的,只有23-25%的书面例子可以回顾. 在"LoCoMo"上,每个内存条件都以同样的拒绝回答. 我们的作家们只经历了MemT-1.0的食谱的前半部分[16]:继续使用原始文字(100M令牌),没有后训练. MemT遵循其20B表示继续预训的标志,使用14B表示的后再再就内存特定数据进行培训,从被冰冻的骨干中提炼出,以完整历史. 这个阶段增加了大约10.69分,它的目标恰恰是使用我们作家缺乏的交叉位置。 热行与其被预先训练的规范相比没有预算,一般输入漂移是[31]的"N-克臂"的1.6倍. 预算将我们限制在一个有N-克表的模型上。 我们没有为LongCat-Flash-Lite(英语:LongCat-Flash-Lite)训练作家,这个由EngramEdit [4]编辑的模型,在输入时添加了它的正克嵌入而无门. 我们也没有为DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017训练一门,它在不同层次上注入了两张桌子. 写作者被捆绑在自己的骨干上,所以每个写作者都需要自己的;第二个写作者也会用一个以上的注射点来测试被捆绑的漂移. 所有结果都来自一个训练种子。

blocks.en: The most likely reason, still to be tested, is the training objective. Raw-text continuation rewards writing, at the row of an n-gram k k , what follows k k , and reading it back at the same position when k k next appears. DEV64 continuation uses memory in exactly this way, which is why it works there. Question answering instead needs information written at the positions of the question’s content to be moved by attention to the answer position, and the writer was never asked to write for that. Two observations point the same way. The 0.6B prototype trained with a question-answering objective answers 16 of 16 facts after one write, against 2 of 16 with empty memory ( Section 6.1 ); after the switch to raw text this ability was not kept. And in [ 31 ] , gradient updates of the same table reached 56.9% on the seven tasks through the same frozen attention. So the table, read through frozen attention, can carry the answers when it is trained with answer gradients. Whether a forward writer trained for cross-position use can reach that, or whether reading across positions also needs a memory module with its own attention, as in MemT-1.0 [ 16 ] , remains open.
blocks.zh: 最可能的原因仍然是培训目标。 Raw-text continuation 奖励了写作, 在 n- gram k k 的行中, 后面的 K k , 当 k k 下一个出现时, 在同一个位置读取它 。 DEV64续作完全以这种方式使用内存,这也是它在那里工作的原因. 相反,回答问题需要用问题内容位置所写的信息,以便通过注意回答位置来移动,而作者从未被要求为此写作. 二观察所指相同. 0.6B原型在一次写完16个事实中的16个事实中接受了回答的客观回答,而16个事实中有2个是空的内存(第6.1节);在切换为原始文本之后,这种能力没有被保留。 在[31]中,同一表格的梯度更新通过同样的被冻结的注意,在7项任务上达到56.9%. 因此,通过被冷冻的注意力读取的表格,在经过解答梯度训练后,可以携带答案. 接受过跨位置使用训练的前置写手能否达到这个目标,或者跨位置读取是否也需要一个有自己关注的内存模块,如"MemT-1.0 [16]"中,仍然开放.

blocks.en: 10 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 10 结论

blocks.en: Delta N-gram writes into a language model’s own N-gram table with forward passes only. It needs no gradients, labels or optimizer state at use time and never touches the pretrained table. A 4M-parameter writer trained on raw text with the pretraining objective learns document-specific memory that survives later writes. A second writer, which reads its own memory while encoding evidence, writes memory that is more specific to its document and drifts less over long chains. Both stay stable over chains of 35,000 writes. Because every change is a patch on a known row, drift can be traced to and intervened on at individual rows, which is what turns a drift budget from a measurement into something that can be enforced. Two problems remain. First, written content is not yet usable at other positions; one explanation still to be tested is that the answer position reads rows the evidence never wrote. Second, a few format rows shared by every example carry both the generic gain and the drift on general inputs. A cross-position training objective, a per-row cap set by the drift budget, and context-keyed slots for hot rows address these two problems; they are the next steps.
blocks.zh: Delta N-gram写入语言模型自己的N-gram表,只写前传. 它在使用时不需要梯度,标签或优化状态,从不触及被预先训练过的表格. 4M参数的写作者接受过原始文字培训,并具有预训目标,学习后来写作中存活下来的特定文档记忆. 第二作人,在将证据编码的同时读取了自己的记忆,写出更具体的内存,并减少被长链所漂移. 两人在三万五千多篇文章的链条上保持稳定。 由于每个变化都是已知行上的一个补丁,漂移可以被追踪到各个行上并进行干涉,这就是将漂移预算从测量变成可以执行的东西. 还有两个问题。 首先,书面内容尚不能在其他位置使用;一个有待测试的解释是,答案位置读取从未写过的证据。 第二,每个例子共用的几行格式既包含一般收益,也包含一般输入的漂移. 一个跨位置的训练目标,由漂移预算设定的每行封顶,以及热排的上下文键入槽来解决这两个问题;它们是下一步.

blocks.en: A.1 Training on Qwen3.8
blocks.zh: A.1 关于Quen3.8的培训

blocks.en: Training uses tensor and pipeline parallelism 1, expert parallelism 4 and data parallelism 4 on four H200 GPUs, with three trajectories per GPU and twelve per update. Gradients are summed across GPUs and normalised once by the number of target tokens in the whole group. The pretrained table holds about 51 billion parameters and is kept in CPU memory.
blocks.zh: 培训在4个H200GPU上使用拉伸和管线平行主义1,专家平行主义4和数据平行主义4,每个GPU有3个轨迹,每个更新有12个. 梯度由跨GPU相接而成,一次由整个组中的目标符数而成常态. 预训表持有约510亿个参数,并保存在CPU内存中.

blocks.en: With T 0 T^{0} -only encoding, H ^ \hat{H} does not depend on the memory, which allows a staged schedule: 1. encode all blocks of all trajectories in one batch; 2. run the D1 write chain block by block; 3. run all queries forward and backward in one batch, giving the gradient of each block’s patch; 4. backpropagate along the write chain into the writer. This reaches 3,000–3,300 target tokens per second, against about 940 for the interleaved schedule. Its loss agrees with the sequential schedule to within 0.001. Gradient differences are at the level of the routing-noise floor below. Memory-aware encoding requires the sequential schedule.
blocks.zh: 只有编码 H^\ hat{H} 并不依赖于内存, 而内存允许一个相机排程 : 1. 将所有轨迹的所有区块编码为一批; 2. 逐个区块运行 D1 写链块; 3. 将所有查询往前和往后运行为一批, 给出每个区块的补丁的梯度; 4. 沿着写链向写入写入. 这达到每秒3 000至3 300个目标符号,而相隔时间约为940个。 它的损失与0.001范围内的相继时间表一致。 梯度差异位于下方的路由-噪声层. 记忆意识编码需要顺序表.

blocks.en: encode all blocks of all trajectories in one batch;
blocks.zh: 将所有轨迹的所有块编码为一批;

blocks.en: run the D1 write chain block by block;
blocks.zh: 逐块运行 D1 写链块;

blocks.en: run all queries forward and backward in one batch, giving the gradient of each block’s patch;
blocks.zh: 将所有查询分为一批进行,并给出每个块的补丁的梯度;

blocks.en: backpropagate along the write chain into the writer.
blocks.zh: 沿着写作链向编剧后推进。

blocks.en: The backbone runs in BF16, and a patch of order 0.01 ⋅ RMS ⁡ ( T 0 ) 0.01\cdot\mathrm{RMS}(T^{0}) added to T 0 T^{0} would mostly be rounded away. The read-out is therefore split into a BF16 projection of the base table and an FP32 projection of the patch, which are added before the injection. The empty patch read through this split branch is the baseline for every comparison; it is not bitwise equal to the original BF16 read-out.
blocks.zh: 骨干以 BF16 为主干线运行,一补丁 0.01 → RMS → (T 0) 0.01\cdot\mathrm{ RMS} (T^{0}) 加入 T 0 T^{0} 后将多被四舍五入. 因此读出后被分为BF16投影底表和FP32投影补丁,在投影前被加入. 通过这个分割分支读取的空补丁是每次比较的基线;它不与原来的 BF16 读出值比对.

blocks.en: With ten of 512 experts active per token, a patch that differs only in its last bits can switch the experts of some tokens. Between such near-identical states the writer’s gradient changes by about 31.6% relative. Schedule equivalence is judged against this floor, not bit equality.
blocks.zh: 512位专家中有10位活跃于每个信使中,一个仅以上个位元相区别的补丁可以切换出一些信使中的专家. 作者的梯度变化大约为31.6%。 附表等同性是根据这个下限来判断的,而不是比特等同.

blocks.en: Two fixes made forward passes with and without gradient tracking bit-identical: fixing the router’s top- k k to sorted order in both modes, and running two fused mixing functions eagerly. Evaluation runs without gradient tracking. With tracking on but no backward pass, the graph accumulated and memory grew from 68 to 143 GB until evaluation stalled; without it, memory stays near 78 GB.
blocks.zh: 两种前行的修饰都经过和不经过梯度跟踪比特-等同:将路由器的上-k-以两种模式排序,并急切地运行两种接合功能。 评价在没有梯度跟踪的情况下进行。 随着追踪但无后传,所积累的图表和内存从68GB增长到143GB,直到评价停滞;没有它,内存会停留在78GB附近.

blocks.en: A.2 Inference with live writes
blocks.zh: A.2 用活写法推论

blocks.en: For generation we extend vLLM’s Qwen3.8 read-out with the same FP32 patch branch. Normalisation, gating and convolution of the read-out run in FP32, and the result is cast to BF16 before it joins the residual stream; the patch is never merged into the BF16 table. Under tensor parallelism 8, one rank computes each D1 update and all ranks adopt its result. The state is updated only between requests. Every request checks the state hash before and after, and answering never modifies the state. Writing a 23,000-token dialogue takes about 12 seconds on A800 GPUs. The state of a 13,000–25,000-token dialogue is 78–145 MB in FP32 without compression.
blocks.zh: 使用相同的FP32补丁分支, FP32中读取运行的常态化,取出并演化,结果被铸入BF16后再加入残流;补丁从未被合并入BF16表. 在收音机平行论8下,一个分级计算每次D1更新,所有分级都采用结果. 状态只在请求之间更新. 每一次请求都会检查前后的散列状态,回答时从未修改过状态. 写出一个2.3万个按键的对话需要大约12秒的A800 GPU. 13,000–25,000-token对话状态为78–145 MB在FP32中不压缩.

blocks.en: A.3 Reproducibility
blocks.zh: A.3 可复制性

blocks.en: Every run is bound to the SHA-256 hashes of its source code, checkpoint and data. Exact resumption of training is allowed only when the code manifest hash matches; a code change goes through a registered migration that leaves the old sources untouched. Generations are sealed before they are scored, and key numbers were recomputed independently from raw per-item records. The DEV64 donor pairs and distractors are fixed by hash before training. The code is available at https://github.com/af-74413592/delta-ngram .
blocks.zh: 每次运行都与它的源代码,检查站和数据的SHA-256散列相接. 只有当代码显示散列匹配时,才允许精确地恢复培训;代码更改会经过注册的迁移,使旧源不受影响. 世代相传被封后再被打出分来,而密钥数被从原始的逐项记录中独立重算出. DEV64型捐赠者对和分心器在训练前由散列固定. 代码见https://github.com/af-74413592/delta-ngram.
